chunks: Sa'd, from Abi Ja'far, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman Mawla Tirbal, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام would perform salat in the masjid, then spit in front of him, to his right, to his left, and behind him upon the pebbles, and he would not cover it.
So the correct view regarding these reports is permissibility and the lifting of prohibition, even though the more virtuous course, according to the previous reports, is to refrain from both.

key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: what is more virtuous or preferable
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the place of worship under discussion
key_terms.عَلَى الْحَصَى: upon the pebbles of the mosque floor

ai.seo_question: Is spitting in the masjid prohibited or merely disliked in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that spitting in the masjid, in the circumstance described, is permissible and not prohibited. However, the concluding legal note states that refraining from it remains more virtuous based on earlier reports, showing a distinction between permissibility and what is preferable.
